correctness.rationale: Derived exact three acute-angle dot-product inequalities for P=(p,0), Q=(q,h(1-q)), R=(-t,h(1-t)). For fixed side parameters q,t>0, eligible p lies in two endpoint strips near -t and q of lengths h^2(1-t)^2/(q+t) and h^2(1-q)^2/(q+t), respectively. Verified uniform 6/(q+t) majorant, integrable on the unit square, and bounded signed scaled mark z to pass from pointwise interval convergence to L1 and conditional total-variation. Independently evaluated the one-variable coefficient integral as 8log2/3-7/6=0.6817258148265. Strict angle boundaries are null, parent height h->0. Full probability result is analytic dominated convergence, not extrapolation from Monte Carlo.
